Reflecting On Online Marketplace Stocks' Q2 Earnings: MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI)

As the Q2 earnings season comes to a close, it's time to take stock of this quarter's best and worst performers in the online marketplace industry, including MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) and its peers.

Marketplaces have existed for centuries. Where once it was a main street in a small town or a mall in the suburbs, sellers benefitted from proximity to one another because they could draw customers by offering convenience and selection. Today, a myriad of online marketplaces fulfill that same role, aggregating large customer bases, which attracts commission-paying sellers, generating flywheel scale effects that feed back into further customer acquisition.

The 11 online marketplace stocks we track reported a satisfactory Q2. As a group, revenues beat analysts' consensus estimates by 1.9% while next quarter's revenue guidance was 1.8% below.

Amidst this news, share prices of the companies have had a rough stretch. On average, they are down 9.6% since the latest earnings results.

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI)

Originally started as an online auction platform, MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) is a one-stop e-commerce marketplace and fintech platform in Latin America.

MercadoLibre reported revenues of $10.17 billion, up 49.8% year on year. This print exceeded analysts' expectations by 4.5%. Overall, it was an exceptional quarter for the company with a solid beat of analysts' EBITDA estimates and impressive growth in its users.

MercadoLibre Total Revenue

MercadoLibre scored the fastest revenue growth in the group. The company reported 89 million daily active users, up 25.4% year on year. Investor expectations, however, were likely higher than Wall Street's published projections, leaving some wishing for even better results (analysts' consensus estimates are those published by big banks and advisory firms, not the investors who make buy and sell decisions). The stock is down 1.6% since reporting and currently trades at $1,892.

Read why we think that MercadoLibre is one of the best online marketplace stocks, our full report is free.

Best Q2: Etsy (NYSE:ETSY)

Founded by a struggling amateur furniture maker Robert Kalin and his two friends, Etsy (NYSE:ETSY) is one of the world's largest online marketplaces, focusing on handmade or vintage items.

Etsy reported revenues of $668.3 million, up 6.2% year on year, outperforming analysts' expectations by 3.4%. The business had an exceptional quarter with a solid beat of analysts' EBITDA estimates.

Etsy Total Revenue

Although it had a fine quarter compared to its peers, the market seems unhappy with the results as the stock is down 11% since reporting. It currently trades at $76.39.

title: MercadoLibre vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
MercadoLibre vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool

The e-commerce landscape is shifting as regional giants and global software leaders battle for market share. Deciding between MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) and Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) requires weighing hyper-local execution against worldwide scale.

MercadoLibre operates a vertically integrated marketplace and payments system tailored for the unique challenges of Latin America. Shopify offers a versatile software infrastructure that enables merchants to build independent brands globally. Both companies are core holdings for investors seeking exposure to digital commerce, but they vary significantly in valuation and regional focus.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a vast ecosystem through its marketplace and its fintech arm, Mercado Pago. Among retail stocks, it differentiates itself by providing logistics and credit solutions to millions of users. The company partners with Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) for its cloud infrastructure while integrating services from Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) into its loyalty programs.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $28.9 billion, representing a significant 39.1% increase over the prior year. This expansion was supported by a net income of approximately $2.0 billion. The company continues to benefit from its dual-engine model, in which its marketplace drives adoption of its financial services, resulting in a net margin of nearly 6.9%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, stands at nearly 1.2x. The debt-to-equity ratio, representing total debt as a proportion of shareholder equity, is roughly 1.7x. Free cash flow, calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, reached nearly $10.8 billion during the same fiscal period.

The case for Shopify

Shopify provides the essential internet infrastructure that allows merchants of all sizes to start, run, and grow their businesses. The platform serves millions of businesses globally, providing tools for sales across web, mobile, and physical locations. It maintains strategic dependencies on Alphabet for cloud hosting and integrates payment services from providers like Stripe and PayPal to streamline merchant operations.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $11.6 billion, marking a growth of approximately 30.1% over the previous twelve months. The company reported a net income of roughly $1.2 billion for the year, achieving a net margin of nearly 10.7%. This growth illustrates the continued demand for independent storefront solutions as more businesses move away from centralized third-party marketplaces.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Shopify has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, indicating negligible debt relative to its shareholders' equity. The current ratio stands at a robust 6.0x, providing significant liquidity for future investments. Free cash flow reached nearly $2.0 billion, though note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.1% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because it is a non-cash expense.

Risk profile comparison

MercadoLibre faces significant risks from intensifying competition, particularly from Asian e-commerce entrants employing aggressive pricing and logistics strategies. The company is sensitive to macro-economic volatility in Latin America, including high inflation and currency devaluations. Regulatory risks are also acute, as its fintech arm operates under varying financial regimes and faces evolving antitrust scrutiny regarding its platform algorithms and logistics integration.

Shopify faces intense competition from established platforms like Amazon and niche providers, with risks amplified by the potential integration of competing technologies. The company is susceptible to macroeconomic downturns, which disproportionately affect its small and medium-sized merchant base. Legal and regulatory risks include evolving privacy laws, potential liability for merchant activities, and reliance on third-party cloud providers and artificial intelligence models for core operations.

Valuation comparison

MercadoLibre offers a lower valuation on both an earnings and sales basis compared to the premium pricing currently assigned to Shopify.

The Forward P/E ratio measures the stock price against its projected future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures the company's market value relative to its sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

To compare MercadoLibre and Shopify, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

To start, there's growth. Let me be clear: Both of these companies have excellent growth. Over the last five years, MercadoLibre has averaged 44% year-over-year revenue growth. Shopify, meanwhile, has averaged 27%. Moreover, these are not small companies. MercadoLibre has generated about $35.2 billion in revenue over the last 12 months; Shopify has recorded about $13.3 billion. Nevertheless, MercadoLibre comes out ahead in the head-to-head comparison given its exceptional revenue growth.

Another factor to consider is each company's valuation. We'll use forward price-to-earnings (P/E) to compare them. MercadoLibre's forward P/E is 49x, which is well above the market average. However, Shopify's 91x forward P/E multiple is not quite double that of MercadoLibre. While both companies are far from value darlings, MercadoLibre gains the edge in this category.

Last, we should take a closer look at each company's balance sheet. In short, both have solid balance sheets. Shopify has over $4.7 billion in net cash, giving it plenty of room for future acquisitions, capital investments, or stock buybacks. MercadoLibre, meanwhile, has around $484 million in net cash, meaning it can easily cover its debt obligations with cash alone.

In summary, both stocks are worthy of serious consideration for growth-oriented investors. However, if forced to choose between the two, I prefer MercadoLibre for its faster growth and relatively more modest valuation.

Key Stats for MercadoLibre Stock

Current Price: $1,892.44

Target Price (Mid): ~$6,290

Street Target: ~$2,270

Potential Total Return: ~232%

Annualized IRR: ~33% / year

What Happened?

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) closed at $1,892.44 on October 12, 2026. That is 9.5% above its September 30 close, a gain that followed a rally in Brazilian assets set off by Brazil's first-round presidential vote. Brazil supplied 52.6% of the company's 2025 revenue, so the stock moved with the country.

Whether to sell into that gain or add to it depends less on the October 25 runoff than on the margin and credit trends management laid out in its Q2 2026 investor relations materials.

A Re-Rating, Not an Upgrade

Flávio Bolsonaro took 47.03% of valid votes to Lula's 45.16% on October 4. The next day, the Ibovespa closed at a record 206,912, up 7.7%, with Brazilian banks leading the rally. MercadoLibre was a secondary beneficiary, trading nearly 8% higher in the October 5 morning session. A Datafolha poll on October 8 showed Bolsonaro ahead 49% to 45%, still a technical tie.

The gain came from the multiple. MercadoLibre's NTM P/E ratio rose from about 41x on September 30 to about 45x on October 12, while consensus NTM EPS held at around $42. Investors are paying more for the same forecast.

The Street is less enthusiastic than the stock price. Between September 30 and October 12, hold ratings rose to six from four out of 26 analysts; the full split is 16 Buy, 4 Outperform, and 6 Hold. The mean target of around $2,270 sits about 20% above the current price.

MercadoLibre NTM Price / Normalized Earnings (P/E) (TIKR)
Lower Rates Would Help, but Only a Little

Lower Brazilian policy rates were already on analysts' minds before the vote; HSBC's Neha Agarwala asked about them on the Q2 call. In reply, Osvaldo Giménez, President of Fintech, said credit and acquiring prices reset with policy rates, so the benefit there is marginal.

The Marketplace gains slightly more, because the company does not reprice its interest-free installment plans as often. CFO Martin de los Santos added: "The Marketplace, typically, when interest rates come down, we improve a little bit margins."

A little is the right size. The Q2 EBIT margin was 6.72%, down from 12.15% a year earlier. The company attributes the decline to deliberate investment, including lower seller take rates in Brazil and higher device costs in acquiring. Rates alone will not close that gap.

Credit is the bigger swing factor. Giménez said that "so far, we are not seeing any deceleration or deterioration of credit book in Brazil." Non-performing loans 15 to 90 days past due sat at 7.0% for the portfolio and 4.6% for credit cards, both near historical lows. The caveat is that loans more than 90 days past due rose in Q2. Management tied that to one product whose early borrowers defaulted above expectations before issuance slowed.

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI is seeing stronger customer engagement as the growing integration between its commerce marketplace and Mercado Pago financial services encourages users to interact more frequently across both platforms. The company's integrated ecosystem is becoming a key driver of customer activity, with shopping, payments, credit offerings and loyalty benefits reinforcing one another. The second quarter of 2026 highlighted this trend, as more customers embraced multiple services within MercadoLibre's ecosystem.

The number of ecosystemic users, who engage with both the marketplace and Mercado Pago, increased 37% year over year. This group has been MercadoLibre's fastest-growing user segment since the fourth quarter of 2023. Compared with marketplace-only users, ecosystemic customers generated 70% more gross merchandise volume and purchased 55% more items per user. Their engagement also spanned product categories, with the share of ecosystemic users purchasing three or more categories exceeding that of marketplace-only users by more than 15 percentage points.

Financial services are strengthening this connection. Total payment volume per ecosystemic user was nearly 90% higher than among fintech-only users, while assets under management per user were more than twice as high. Mercado Pago credit cardholders were also two to three times more likely to remain ecosystemic. Contribution profit per ecosystemic user was multiples of the combined profit generated by marketplace-only and fintech-only users.

MELI+ subscriber growth increased 72% year over year, adding another layer of engagement. These trends demonstrate how MercadoLibre's interconnected offerings are fostering deeper customer relationships and reinforcing the engagement flywheel.

How Does MercadoLibre Stack Up Against Its Industry?

MercadoLibre, which competes with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN and Sea Limited SE, has seen its shares rise 1.2% over the past three months compared with the industry's 3.1% growth. While Amazon shares have climbed 6.1%, Sea Limited has fallen 14% in the aforementioned period.

title: MercadoLibre (MELI) Trades Profit for Scale. Smart Bet or Warning?

MercadoLibre (MELI) Trades Profit for Scale. Smart Bet or Warning?
Maham Fatima
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 8:25 AM MDT 5 min read
MELI
Trade MELI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) posted a quarter that looks like two different companies stapled together. In its fiscal second quarter of 2026, net revenue and financial income jumped 50% to $10,169 million. Income from operations fell 17% to $683 million. Management described the profit squeeze as a deliberate choice to plow operating leverage back into its value proposition.

MercadoLibre is the region's best-known online marketplace, plus a lot more. It earns commissions and shipping fees on goods sold, sells ads to merchants, and runs Mercado Pago, a fintech arm that processes payments, holds deposits, and lends money. Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina are its biggest markets.

So the real question is whether investors are watching a company invest in a wider moat, or one that has to pay more just to keep growing. The answer depends on what that spending is actually buying, a dynamic long-term investors weigh when eyeing transformative secular plays like the 10 Stocks That Will Change the World by 2030.

MercadoLibre (MELI) Trades Profit for Scale. Smart Bet or Warning?
An Ecosystem That Feeds Itself

MercadoLibre's edge isn't any single business. It's how the pieces push customers into one another. Shoppers who pay with Mercado Pago become borrowers, borrowers come back to shop, and sellers follow the traffic. The user numbers show that loop working. Unique active buyers reached 89 million in the second quarter, up from 71 million a year earlier. Fintech monthly active users climbed to 88 million from 68 million.

Advertising is the newest layer. Ad revenue grew 62% on an FX-neutral basis (stripping out currency swings), and the company says Mercado Ads topped a 10% share of Latin America's digital ad market for the first time. Selling space to merchants who already depend on the platform is the same retail-media logic behind Amazon's advertising business.

Cheaper Shipping, More Orders

The biggest bet is in Brazil. MercadoLibre lowered its free-shipping threshold there last year, and the payoff is visible in volume. Brazilian items sold rose 56% year over year in the second quarter, while gross merchandise volume (the total value of goods sold) grew 39% FX-neutral.

Company-wide, items sold hit 795 million, up from 550 million. The catch is cost. Higher shipping expenses weren't fully offset by revenue, which squeezed gross margin. Still, the company says free and slow shipments are now contribution-positive across half of the R$19 to R$79 price range, a sign the cheaper orders are starting to pay their own way.

Lending is the other engine. The credit portfolio passed $16 billion, up 75%, and 2.6 million new credit cards went out during the quarter. That push puts it alongside 10 Most Promising Fintech Stocks to Buy Now. NIMAL (net interest margin after losses) slipped to 20.7% from 23.0% a year ago, but improved 3 percentage points from the prior quarter.

XLP rose 3.6%, ending a seven-week losing streak, while XLY gained 2.55%, breaking an eight-week slide.

Planet Fitness climbed13% as UBS said investor sentiment looks "far worse" than fundamentals.

Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, well below the 5,900 analysts expected.

Consumer stocks finally caught a break last week, with both major sector ETFs snapping long losing streaks. Planet Fitness (PLNT), MercadoLibre (MELI) and Genius Sports (GENI) led the advance on analyst support and institutional buying. Polestar Automotive (PSNY), Lucid Group (LCID) and Levi Strauss (LEVI) declined as earnings and delivery reports disappointed.

During the week of Oct. 5 to Oct. 9, the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLP) rose 3.6%, reversing seven straight weeks of losses. The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY) gained 2.55%, ending an eight-week skid.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Both funds outpaced the broader market. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) advanced 1.16%, while the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) edged up 0.23%.

Planet Fitness, MercadoLibre, Genius Sports Among Leading Gainers

Planet Fitness stock rose 13% and posted its best week since May after UBS said investor sentiment looks "far worse" than the company's fundamentals heading into its third-quarter earnings report. The firm said that against a "deteriorating sentiment backdrop," the fitness chain's fundamentals have actually improved. UBS data show strong member growth in September and continued strength in early October.

The analyst called the risk from agentic AI "sensible but manageable in practice" and said Planet Fitness' pricing promotion has been a success. UBS maintained a 'Buy' rating and an $80 price target.

MercadoLibre stock rallied over 11% to its best week in over two years as investors reacted to the first round of Brazil's presidential election. Traders are weighing how potential shifts in regulation and economic conditions could affect the company's largest market, and positioning ahead of anticipated policy impacts.

Susquehanna raised its price target to $2,500 from $2,400 and kept a 'Positive' rating. The firm said that although MercadoLibre continues to invest in developing the market for its products and services, changes in its consumer credit book may begin to lift consolidated EBIT margins. Those margins have fallen year-on-year every quarter since 2023.

Genius Sports stock also advanced over 10% during the week as Cathie Wood's ARK Investment kept buying. The firm picked up 425,800 shares on Oct. 6 and another 347,800 shares on Oct. 8.

Polestar, Lucid, Levi Strauss Decline

Polestar stock posted a weekly decline of 15% as Barclays cut its price target to $5 from $15 and kept an 'Underweight' rating. The cut was part of a Q3 earnings preview for the autos and mobility group. The analyst said macro challenges in 2027 reinforce a preference for U.S. exposure.

Lucid Group produced 2,954 vehicles and delivered 3,806 in Q3. Deliveries exceeded production as the company reduced its existing inventory as part of a plan to improve cash flow by $1.4 billion in 2026.

The numbers still missed. FactSet estimates stood at 3,497 for production and 5,900 for deliveries. StoneX, which has a 'Hold' rating, said the "substantial delivery shortfall underscores the challenge of improving sell-through." BNP Paribas analyst James Picariello called the report "lackluster" and said Lucid faces a "long and difficult journey" to improve operations and drive demand. Lucid stock fell over 8% during the week.

Levi Strauss stock declined nearly 6% last week after the denim maker raised its profit outlook, largely on tariff refunds, but trimmed its revenue guidance. Adjusted full-year EPS is now expected at $1.54 to $1.56, up from $1.46 to $1.52. That's above the $1.49 analysts expected, according to Fiscal.ai data. Net revenue growth guidance was lowered to 7%, the bottom of the prior 7% to 7.5% range, while organic growth is expected at 6%.

In Q3, tariff refunds helped boost Levi Strauss' operating margin by 4.9 percentage points to 13.8%. U.S. revenue fell 1%, while comparable sales from its own stores and website were nearly unchanged. CEO Michelle Gass said direct sales fell below expectations, and the company has already started taking steps to improve results.

Raymond James cut its price target to $22 from $24 but kept an 'Outperform' rating, saying course corrections and improved weather point to a better Q4. JPMorgan trimmed its target to $33 from $34 and kept an Overweight rating, calling the report mixed but the multi-year growth outlook intact.

MercadoLibre (MELI) is back in focus after a recent trading session in which the share price outpaced the broader market, drawing increased attention to upcoming earnings and the company's expanding cross-border logistics network in Latin America.

Recent trading tells a mixed story for MercadoLibre. The latest 7 day share price return of 11.39% and a positive 90 day move of 1.21% suggest short term momentum is building, even though the year to date share price return is down 4.25% and the 1 year total shareholder return is down 11.43%. The 3 year total shareholder return is up 54.46% and the 5 year total shareholder return is up 20.90%.

The recent jump in MercadoLibre's share price now meets a wide gap between where the market prices the stock and where various value estimates cluster. Is that spread signaling opportunity or a warning on fair value?

Most Popular Narrative: 41% Undervalued

On Simply Wall St, the most followed valuation narrative pegs MercadoLibre's fair value at $3,219 per share, well above the latest close of $1,889.85. This frames today's price as a sizeable discount before you even get to the fine print of how that number is built.

The newer map recognized three creatures living inside one business: the merchant, the money mover, and the lender. Separating them made the economics easier to interrogate. It also exposed a complication behind MercadoLibre's magnificent growth.

See why 148 investors see MercadoLibre as 41% undervalued.

According to John_Eric, that split narrative rests on MercadoLibre's marketplace, non credit fintech, and lending operations being valued separately, then recombined into a single estimate. The author's segmented scenarios cluster around a base case of $3,219 per share, with proposed bear and bull variations of $2,950 and $3,822, all using an 11.45% discount rate.

What matters for you as a shareholder or potential investor is how that framework treats the credit book and its funding needs. The lending operation pulls in revenue and net interest margin, yet it also ties up capital and uses higher risk funding sources. This can compress free cash flow even while earnings forecasts point to 28.4% annual growth and revenue projections of 21.3% a year.

The same narrative flags that while the SWS DCF model currently points to an intrinsic value of $3,496.96 per share, any shift in loan performance, funding costs or profit margins could move that estimate. MercadoLibre's recent revenue of $35.2b, net income of $1.9b, and value score of 3 are all ingredients in that broader picture rather than a verdict on their own.

Result: Fair Value of $3,219 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, MercadoLibre's lending and fintech funding needs, along with any shift in loan performance or margins, could quickly challenge that view of the shares as 41% undervalued.

Another View: MercadoLibre Through The Earnings Lens

While the popular narrative frames MercadoLibre as 41% undervalued on a segmented fair value of $3,219 per share, the earnings multiple sends a different message. At a P/E of 51.4x versus a peer average of 20.8x and a fair ratio of 32.7x, the stock screens expensive. Is that premium cushioning risk or stretching it?

Can MercadoLibre's Cross-Border Trade Drive Its Next Growth Phase?

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI is strengthening its e-commerce presence across Latin America, supported by robust cross-border trade (CBT) growth and investments in fulfillment capabilities. The company's expanding international seller network is broadening product selection, improving pricing competitiveness and enhancing the shopping experience. These initiatives are emerging as key growth drivers for its marketplace business.

Cross-border trade maintained strong momentum in the second quarter of 2026, with foreign-exchange-neutral gross merchandise volume (GMV) up 60% year over year. Mexico remained MercadoLibre's largest CBT market, with growth well above the country's overall marketplace average. Meanwhile, Argentina, Brazil, and other markets recorded triple-digit CBT growth. In smaller markets, CBT's share of GMV nearly doubled from the year-ago period, reflecting broader adoption.

MercadoLibre's China fulfillment center is playing an increasingly important role in this expansion. The facility now serves thousands of sellers, with shipment volume rising 170% sequentially during the quarter. The fulfillment infrastructure has enabled faster deliveries and fewer cancellations, supporting stronger customer satisfaction, retention, and repeat purchases.

Cross-border trade offers MercadoLibre opportunities to strengthen marketplace engagement by expanding access to competitively priced products across categories. Continued improvements in fulfillment efficiency, seller participation, and delivery reliability should help attract more buyers and encourage repeat purchases. Although the initiative remains in its early stages, improving economics and a growing contribution position CBT as a promising long-term growth lever.

How Does MercadoLibre Stack Up Against Its Industry?

MercadoLibre, which competes with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN and Sea Limited SE, has seen its shares rise 0.3% over the past three months compared with the industry's 2.1% increase. While Amazon shares have climbed 3.6%, Sea Limited has fallen 16.4% in the aforementioned period.

What Does MercadoLibre's Current Valuation Suggest?

From a valuation standpoint, MercadoLibre's forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 36.25, higher than the industry average of 20.21. The stock is also trading above its 12-month median level of 34.18.

MercadoLibre is trading at a premium to Amazon (forward 12-month P/E of 22.83) and Sea Limited (18.37).

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Do Earnings Estimates Signal for MercadoLibre?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MercadoLibre's current fiscal-year sales implies 44.7% year-over-year growth, while the consensus estimate for earnings per share suggests a 2.8% decline. For the next fiscal year, the consensus estimate indicates a 29% rise in sales and 43.7% growth in earnings.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

MELI Investment Case

MercadoLibre's strong e-commerce momentum, expanding cross-border trade and growing fintech ecosystem reinforce its long-term growth prospects. Rising user engagement, advertising growth and credit portfolio expansion remain key positives. However, margin compression from strategic investments, higher logistics costs and softer consumer demand in certain markets warrant caution. MELI currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). title: The Ultimate Buy-and-Hold Stock for the Next 20 Years

The Ultimate Buy-and-Hold Stock for the Next 20 Years
Will Healy, The Motley Fool

Picking a stock to buy and hold for 20 years is a risky proposition, no matter how conservative the stock. A lot can happen in that time, and what may look like an impenetrable competitive advantage in one decade could disappear by the next.

That said, MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI) may just be a stock worth putting in your long-haul buy-and-hold portfolio. Its diverse digital businesses, which thrive on synergies, should make the consumer discretionary stock a winner for at least 20 years.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
The strengths of MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre has combined businesses such as e-commerce, fintech, and logistics into a single operation. These enterprises work both separately and together to capitalize on opportunities.

One common reason why some hesitate to invest in MercadoLibre is that it operates in Latin America, a region often subjected to political and economic turmoil. Still, MercadoLibre is also adept at turning the region's challenges into opportunities.

Because so many people in its core markets lacked access to digital payment options, it chose to form its own fintech business, Mercado Pago. This has given millions of previously unbanked customers a way to participate in the financial system. Additionally, the lack of fulfillment and shipping options in Latin America led the company to create Mercado Envios, a business that brought next-day delivery and other services to the region.

This integrated approach is working. MercadoLibre booked revenue of $19 billion in the first half of 2026, a 50% year-over-year increase. Despite that massive improvement, its net income fell by 13% to $883 million over the same period. This was in part because the company's e-commerce margins shrank as competition increased. It also had to increase its allowance for non-performing loans as its loan book grew dramatically.

However, long-term investors should appreciate that it is foregoing some profits now to grow its business for the long term. Its lower e-commerce margins today will likely lead to less competition later, which should allow it to increase its market share. Also, as it becomes better at evaluating borrowers, its growing loan book will probably benefit the company's bottom line.

Furthermore, MercadoLibre compares well with other e-commerce stocks such as Amazon. MercadoLibre's market cap is about $94 billion, a tiny fraction of Amazon's $2.8 trillion market cap. While there are no guarantees, Amazon's history may hint at MercadoLibre's future as it captures more of its addressable market.
